mechanisms.name: typert-descriptor-codegen
mechanisms.what: Build-time generation plus runtime manifest loading of the strict Typert Remote descriptors that everything else dispatches against. `typertPlugin()` is a rolldown/tsdown plugin named `dsh-typert-generator` that lowers source decorators (target ES2024) and, in writeBundle, emits local and Host-for-Client artifacts; the workspace analyzer batches package analysis (batchSize 8) and the Cordis catalog projector truncates any declaration longer than MAX_DECL_CHARS = 1500 into a stub. At runtime the `typert-loader` plugin (inject ['typert','loader']) resolves each package.json `exports["./typert"]` target, dynamically imports it, and validates the `TYPERT` manifest via validateTypertManifest before calling ctx.typert.register. The generator package itself has no Cordis plugin row; it is build tooling.
invariants: The generated descriptor version is 1; a prototype descriptor with any other version throws rather than being coerced (typert/protocol readRemoteMethodDescriptor).
A `./typert` manifest must be owned by the exact package that exports it (manifest.package === pkgName) and must declare face 'host'.
Only public instance methods with string names may carry Remote markers; decorators on private/static/symbol members throw.
constants: MAX_DECL_CHARS = 1500 (declarations longer than this render as a truncated stub)

mechanisms.name: typert-remote-rpc-plane
mechanisms.what: The primary command/API surface of dsh is a Remote method-invocation plane, not a slash-command surface. `@Remote`/`@RemoteScope` decorators record versioned method markers on the class prototype; `TypertRemoteService` binds a Cordis service key to a wire namespace; TypertRegistry (`super(ctx, 'typert')`) holds the local/remote/lookup/context descriptor stores. `TypertGatewayService` (`super(ctx, 'typertGateway')`) intercepts the shared `/api` Connection channel, claims endpoints, and dispatches through `prepareInvocation` -> `Reflect.apply`, falling back to conservative SRC descriptors derived from `Function.prototype.toString` parameter parsing when no strict definition exists. Failures ride one `RemoteError` class discriminated by `code`, never by instanceof.
invariants: Endpoint grammar is exactly two segments `<namespace>/<method>` sharing the Connection segment pattern /^[A-Za-z0-9_$.-]+$/ with '.' and '..' rejected.
Once an endpoint's strict definition has been seen (hasSeen), SRC fallback is forbidden for it forever.
Argument objects must match the descriptor exactly: extra fields and non-omissible missing fields are refused; lookup ids are never omissible.
constants: Universal gateway error codes: gateway/bad-request, gateway/cancelled, gateway/internal (plus 17 gateway infrastructure codes merged by remote-error-codes.ts)

mechanisms.name: browser-http-api-transport
mechanisms.what: The HTTP carrier for browser and non-browser consumers. `client-connection` registers a `prefix` route at API_PATH '/api' on the webServer, bridges node:http to a WHATWG fetch handler with chunked backpressure and client-disconnect abort, and exposes a carrier-neutral registry (`ctx.connection.rpc.handle/intercept`, `ctx.connection.fetch.register`) plus `requestRejection`/`authorizeIndex` for other host routes. Exact Fetch routes registered through `ctx.connection.fetch` reuse the same fence and body cap. `host/open-in-app` is the in-tree consumer of that reused fence for its three routes.
invariants: One interceptor per channel: a second `intercept('/api', ...)` throws; the reserved channel '/api' may not be registered as a normal channel.
Buffered request bodies are capped before dispatch; the cap must be at least ceil(aggregate image limit * 4/3) + 1 MiB envelope headroom or plugin load fails.
Client-disconnect detection hangs off ServerResponse 'close' (not IncomingMessage 'close'), gated on writableEnded.

mechanisms.name: service-self-auth-token-cookie
mechanisms.what: Authentication of the service itself (not of the model provider). One process launch token is minted per root context and printed as `?token=` on the URL the launcher hands the operator; `authorizeIndex` exchanges a valid single GET / token for an HMAC-SHA256-signed, authority-bound cookie (`v1.<body>.<sig>`, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/), 303-redirecting to clean '/'. Every /api request is then checked by `isAuthenticated`, which verifies the signature, the exact Host-derived authority in the payload, and the issued/expires window. The durable signing secret is a 32-byte base64url value stored as a `grant` credential record under credentialKey('client-connection','browser-session').
invariants: Cookie name is sha256(authority)-derived with the `dsh-auth-` prefix, so one Host cannot present another Host's cookie; the payload authority must also equal the request authority.
Discrimination is by the app-level authority comparison, and both token and signature comparisons are length-checked timingSafeEqual.
The failure response is always the same minimal 401 text; no state distinguishes bad token from bad cookie.

mechanisms.name: browser-trust-fence
mechanisms.what: The pre-dispatch authority fence that every /api request passes before authentication: `isTrustedApiRequest` requires a parsable Host whose hostname is loopback or a declared `trustedHosts` authority, refuses any `sec-fetch-site: cross-site` marker, and, when an Origin is attached, requires it to normalize to exactly the Host authority. Loopback covers localhost/[::1] and 127/8; a port-less `trustedHosts` entry matches any port while an explicit `host:port` entry matches exactly. Config entries are validated at plugin load by `assertTrustedAuthority` so a typo fails the fiber instead of silently widening trust.
invariants: The Host fence applies to every request, browser-looking or not; there is deliberately no marker shortcut, because a plain-HTTP browser read carries neither Origin nor Fetch-Metadata.
A configured entry must survive WHATWG parsing unchanged (canonicalization aside) or plugin load throws.
The fence is explicitly not an auth layer; network binding belongs to webserver config and authentication to BrowserAuth.
constants: HTTP 403 for a failed fence, 401 for a failed authentication (checked in that order)

mechanisms.name: remote-stream-websocket-mux
mechanisms.what: Streaming Remote methods (mode: 'stream') do not use HTTP request/response; they ride one WebSocket mux owned by the Gateway. `RemoteStreamMuxServer` is a noServer WebSocketServer mounted on the webServer upgrade route REMOTE_STREAM_MUX_PATH '/api/remote.mux'; it applies the Connection rejection before upgrading, multiplexes many logical streams per socket, and reaps dead peers with Ping/Pong heartbeats (MAX_MISSED_HEARTBEATS = 2 at the configured interval). The Gateway's `stream()` method validates that the descriptor is stream-mode and wraps the returned iterable in `cancellableStream`, which races iterator.next() against the abort signal.
invariants: One logical stream id is owned once per connection; a duplicate open is rejected and binary frames close the socket with 1003.
A unary method opened through the stream carrier (or a stream method invoked as unary) is gateway/signature-invalid, never silently coerced.
Socket close aborts every active stream and awaits each iterator's return before the connection task settles.

mechanisms.name: forwarded-host-event-bridge
mechanisms.what: The push half of the Remote plane: a single application-selected allowlist of Cordis Host events is forwarded to browser consumers so they can react to server-side state instead of polling. `API_REMOTE_FORWARDED_EVENTS` declares 19 entries with an explicit dispatch mode — 17 `emit` and 2 `waterfall` (`approval/request`, `user-questions/request`) — and is the sole declaration read by both compiler faces and by `ctx.remote.$on`'s legal key set. `api/remotes` turns each entry into a queue-backed AsyncIterable handed to `typertGateway.registerRemoteEvents`; the Gateway opens one `$events` stream per client generation, emits a `ready` frame carrying the clientId and Host facts, correlates waterfall deliveries by eventId, and accepts outcomes back over the `$events/result` unary endpoint.
invariants: A forwarded event name must be non-empty and its arguments must be lossless JSON; a non-JSON argument throws rather than shipping a lossy frame.
Only one forwarded-event source may be registered per Gateway; a second registration throws.
A scoped waterfall delivery must carry its Agent directly and the carrier Agent must be that exact object; otherwise it throws instead of guessing lineage.

mechanisms.name: sdk-jsonrpc-stdio-runtime
mechanisms.what: The out-of-process programmatic wire contract. `JsonRpcLineTransport` speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over caller-owned byte streams with a strict frame discriminator (id+method = request, id = response, method = notification), ignores malformed lines, and answers missing handlers with -32601 and handler failures with -32603. `HarnessSdkJsonRpcServer` implements exactly three request methods (`initialize`, `session/prompt`, `shutdown`) and four server notifications (`session.event`, `session.status`, `subagent.started`, `subagent.finished`), advertising the wire-stable identity `deepseek-harness-sdk-runtime`. The `HarnessClient` is the Node-side driver: it spawns `dsh --profile sdk`, fans notifications out to filtered subscriptions, and tears the child down through a stdin-EOF -> SIGTERM -> SIGKILL ladder.
invariants: The server handshake identity stays the wire-stable name 'deepseek-harness-sdk-runtime'; reinitialization is unsupported.
`session/prompt` only reports in-process subagent runs; remote child runs are never reported as `subagent.finished`.
A timed-out request is an abandonment: the transport drops its pending entry, but the server-side work keeps running until close (there is no wire-level cancel).
constants: JSON-RPC error codes -32601 (method not found) and -32603 (handler failure)
shutdown request timeout default 1000 ms; dispose EOF grace 6000 ms; dispose kill grace 3000 ms

mechanisms.name: acp-agent-client-protocol
mechanisms.what: A second, independent external wire contract: an Agent Client Protocol server over JSON-RPC stdio for automation clients (the `acp` plugin, `dsh --profile acp`). It uses the upstream `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` `ndJsonStream` + `agent()` app and implements initialize, session/new, session/list, session/resume, session/close, session/setConfigOption, session/prompt and the session/cancel notification. Session listing is keyset-paginated with an opaque canonical base64url cursor, resume is refused for subagent-origin or child sessions and requires a physically identical cwd, and permission requests are downgraded to one-shot allow-once/reject-once choices so an unknown client response can never become a durable grant.
invariants: `additionalDirectories` is rejected as outside the automation contract; cwd must be an absolute path.
A durable session is only resumable when it is not subagent-origin, has no parentSession, and its recorded cwd resolves to the same physical directory.
The session/list cursor must be canonical (re-encoding the decoded JSON must reproduce the token byte for byte).

mechanisms.name: web-host-static-and-launch
mechanisms.what: The browser-facing host surface: `WebServer` (`super(ctx, 'webServer')`) is a node:http route registry with exact/prefix matching (longest prefix wins), a single fallback seat, exact-path upgrade routes, optional gzip with a negotiated Accept-Encoding, a structured index-injection table collected per render, and raw `tapIndex` escape hatches. `frontend-static` claims the fallback seat to serve the built SPA dist (403 on traversal outside the dist root, 404 for absent targets, 405 for non-GET/HEAD, octet-stream for unknown extensions) and routes every index response through Connection's authentication then the webserver's index render. The `web-app` bundle supplies the dist location, LAN trust snapshot, canonical URL line, default-browser handoff, `DSH_WEB_URL` shell variable and the model-visible surface prompt.
invariants: Duplicate (kind, path) routes, duplicate upgrade paths and a second fallback registration all throw: route patterns are a composition-level contract.
An upgraded socket is tracked and destroyed explicitly on teardown because Node's closeAllConnections() does not include it.
Index responses always pass Connection authorization before bytes are read; non-index assets stay public.
constants: compression default 'none'; compressionLevel default 1 (0-9); compressionThresholdBytes default 1024
Config.host is one of '127.0.0.1' | '0.0.0.0'; Config.port max 65535 and required (0 = OS-assigned)
default web port 3080 (cordis.patch.yml: `port: !!js ctx.webStartup.port ?? 3080`, not in src)

mechanisms.name: profile-boot-and-cmdline-seam
mechanisms.what: How a dsh service process comes up and who owns the command line. `boot()` resolves the harness home, layers environment (DSH_/XDG_/DYLD_/BASH_FUNC_ bootstrap plus .env), mounts the root include, awaits the Loader and audits activation; `installFailLoud` converts a late unhandled plugin-init rejection into one labelled diagnostic and exit(1). Profiles are directory-shaped: PROFILE_TEMPLATES ships acp/web/headless/sdk/sdk-minimal bundle tuples with per-profile patch reload ('live' for web, 'startup' otherwise) and PROFILE_PATCH_FILENAME 'cordis.patch.yml' is the user layer. The `cmdline` library provides `cmdlineArgs`/`appExit`/`appReady` on the root context so a launcher parses only its own flags and hands the rest to the tree verbatim; `parseCmdline` wires commander help/version/parse failures to `ctx.appExit` structurally (never instanceof), and `exitOnStdinEnd` binds stdio EOF to a bounded successful shutdown.
invariants: App rows never own launcher-level command-line status; the launcher parses its flags and hands everything after them to the tree in argv order.
Commander control-flow errors are detected structurally by a 'commander.'-prefixed code plus a numeric exitCode, because an out-of-tree plugin brings its own commander copy.
A stdio application's EOF must not mask a startup rejection: exit is requested only after AppReady commits.
constants: Fiber state mirrors FIBER_PENDING = 0, FIBER_ACTIVE = 2, FIBER_FAILED = 3

mechanisms.name: settings-and-credentials-rpc-namespace
mechanisms.what: The configuration plane exposed to external consumers as two Typert Remote namespaces on one service: `SettingsController` registers `super(ctx, 'settingsController', { namespace: 'settings' })` and mounts `CredentialsController` as its own plugin (`namespace: 'credentials'`). Reads go through `describe({ redactSecrets: true })` and are projected field by field onto a wire view, so a provider's extra enumerable properties or a `role('secret')` field cannot ride a response. Writes expose merge (`update`), wholesale replacement (`replace`) and path-addressed `mutate` with an optional `expectedRevision`; a stale writer is classified as `settings/conflict` (carrying expected/actual) rather than a malformed request. Two further Remotes open the settings document and a user-authored agent preset directory in native editors.
invariants: Both namespaces stay registered even when no provider is mounted, so a call returns an actionable missing-provider diagnostic instead of a 404.
Every remote read uses redactSecrets: true; secret fields must never be serialized onto the wire.
Credentials describe requests are bounded to 64 refs, and only the declared fields are copied out of a provider answer.

mechanisms.name: command-catalog-rpc-and-lifecycle
mechanisms.what: dsh keeps a real (but non-central) command registry for human-facing operations, exposed as Remote methods rather than as a protocol-level slash surface. `CommandRuntime` (`super(ctx, 'commands')`) merges global and calling-agent-scoped layers, validates and freezes definitions (name pattern, non-empty description, handler type), and exposes `@Remote list(agent)` and `@Remote execute(agent, line, attachments, signal)`. Execution logs a paired `command/run` / `command/done` lifecycle into the session log, admits attachments only when the definition declares `input.attachments`, honours cancellation before the handler runs, and contains `command/done` append failure on the handler-failure path so the handler's own error stays the reported one.
invariants: Command names must match /^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$/ and are the registry key: a duplicate in one layer throws, and a scoped layer shadows the global one.
Admission misses (bad syntax or unknown name) return undefined and log nothing; they never entered a handler.
Minted command ids are instance-token-prefixed (cmd-<8 hex>-<n>) so a resumed log never repeats a pairing id.

mechanisms.name: directory-picker-capability-seam
mechanisms.what: A deliberately capability-shaped (not method-shaped) host service for choosing a workspace directory. `DirectoryPicker` (`super(ctx, 'directoryPicker')`) is abstract and exposes one `capability()` returning a discriminated, merge-extensible union: a `native` backend opens one OS chooser on the host display, a `browse` backend serves one-level listing plus child creation for an in-app browser. The browse side is bounded (maxEntries default 1000, `truncated` flags a cut level) and requires fully qualified paths so a wire value never resolves against the host cwd or current drive. `directory-picker-auto` resolves once at boot which backend to mount by sampling bind host, SSH launch, platform and display availability, mounting the matching backend and surface packages as real Loader entries.
invariants: The capability object must be stable for the service lifetime; consumers may capture it across calls.
An unknown capability kind is documented to hide the picking affordance, not to fail.
Only one implementation may register `ctx.directoryPicker` (normal Cordis duplicate-service behaviour).
constants: Linux chooser binaries ['zenity','kdialog']; Windows dialog CLOSE_RETRY_MS = 150, CLOSE_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 20

mechanisms.name: webhook-ingress-and-verification
mechanisms.what: An inbound ingress surface for external systems, separate from the authenticated browser transport. `WebhookRuntime` (`super(ctx, 'webhookRuntime')`) is a rule registry keyed by provider `kind`: `dispatch` snapshots and deep-freezes the delivery, starts every matching rule fire-and-forget, and the runtime's only built-in action is creating a Workspace-backed session. `webhook-github` registers an exact POST route that requires `application/json` (with at most one UTF-8 charset parameter), reads a bounded body, requires exactly one each of `x-hub-signature-256`, `x-github-delivery` and `x-github-event`, resolves the shared secret from the credential provider, verifies the HMAC through Octokit, dispatches, and answers 202 after in-memory dispatch rather than after rule settlement.
invariants: Rule callbacks are contained: a failing invocation logs and never escapes; a registration disposer hides the rule, aborts it, then drains its active callbacks.
A delivery must be lossless JSON and carry non-empty kind/source/deliveryId and a non-negative safe-integer receivedAt; otherwise dispatch throws synchronously.
Ingress answers are not authorization: the response deliberately carries no verification detail to the sender, and an unavailable secret is a 503, not a 401.
constants: HTTP 202 accepted, 400 bad JSON/header, 401 invalid signature, 405 method, 413 body too large, 415 content type, 503 unavailable
webhook-github maxBodyBytes is required with no default (min 1, max Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)
No numeric constants in webhook/webhook src

mechanisms.name: session-event-stream-contract
mechanisms.what: The event/stream contract a renderer consumes. `MutableSessionEventSource` implements `SessionEventSource` (an ObservableSnapshot of a `SessionEventWindow`) and is the client-side owner of one Session's contiguous event window. The window carries `entries`, `hasMore`, a monotonic `revision`, and the exact `SessionEventChange` delta that produced that revision ('replace' | 'prepend' | 'append' | 'settle-assistant'). Entries are `SessionEventLikeEntry`: durable Session events plus a client-only `assistant/live-chunk` transient frame carrying an attemptId. The window is a persistent concat tree materialized lazily, so prepend/append publish synchronously without copying the whole history.
invariants: Every accepted window mutation publishes synchronously through notifySubscribers; a renderer never sees a torn window.
`revision` increases by exactly one per publish; `change` always describes the delta between the previous and current revision.
A `settle-assistant` removes all transient rows for one attemptId and, when a durable settlement is supplied, inserts it at the first position whose seq is greater.
constants: initial revision = 0; initial window = { hasMore: false, change: { kind: 'replace', entries: [] } }

mechanisms.name: session-wire-event-acceptance
mechanisms.what: The boundary check that keeps a wire page or follow frame from entering the window contract unvalidated. `assertSessionWireEvent` narrows one value received in a follow frame or a history page: it rejects any field outside the seven-name envelope (type, seq, time, data, ignorable, surfaceOp, sourceEventSeqs), requires a non-negative safe-integer seq (rejecting -0), an integer time, a present non-undefined data, and `ignorable` only when literally true, then runs the session package's own `validateSurfaceMetadata` and `validateSessionEventData`. It deliberately does not strip or normalize wire fields, and range membership plus source existence stay Host-owned.
invariants: Event names and payloads are merge-extensible; only event-local owner rules run at this boundary.
An unexpected envelope field is an error, never silently dropped or ignored.
seq and time must be safe integers; -0 is rejected explicitly.
constants: Envelope keys: type, seq, time, data, ignorable, surfaceOp, sourceEventSeqs

mechanisms.name: forwarded-event-subscription-contract
mechanisms.what: The subscription half of the renderer seam: `ctx.remote.$on(event, listener)` lets a client renderer subscribe to a Host Cordis event by its declared name, with the listener type projected from the owner package's own `Events` declaration rather than a flattened restatement. The legal key set is exactly the Host assembly's `API_REMOTE_FORWARDED_EVENTS` allowlist, surfaced to consumers only when `TypertRemoteEventSelection` is augmented by the consumer face. Notifications run in registration order and isolate failures; scoped waterfalls receive the resolved Client Context and may return, delegate through next(), or reject the Host dispatch.
invariants: Nothing is forwarded unless the Host assembly allowlisted it; a consumer face that omits the selection augmentation makes `TypertRemoteEvent` never, so `$on` fails to compile rather than silently no-op.
Only two dispatch modes exist: unscoped void `emit` and scoped async `waterfall` whose last parameter is a same-result next().
A listener's disposer is owned by the calling fiber.

mechanisms.name: client-remote-stream-supervision
mechanisms.what: The client-side stream contract for a renderer that must survive reconnects. `ctx.remote.$stream(options)` returns a single-consumer `RemoteStream<Item>` carrying a physical generation id and a revision; three specializations sit under one abstract `RemoteJournalStream`: journal (change feed), snapshot, and remote. Reconnection is driven by `ConnectionController`, which owns generation/attempt counters privately, computes an exponential backoff cap (`min(backoffMaxMs, base * factor^(attempt-1))`) with 50-100% jitter, exposes state 'connected' | 'disconnected' | 'connecting', and warns if a generation takes longer than generationReadyWarnMs while failing at generationReadyTimeoutMs. `ctx.remote.$host` exposes fixed Host facts (home, isLoopback) as plain identity-stable reads.
invariants: A stream is single-consumer; a replayed frame cannot regress the revision.
constants: backoffBaseMs default 500; backoffFactor default 2; backoffMaxMs default 10000
retry delay is uniformly 50-100% of the current cap

mechanisms.name: session-projection-consumer-contract
mechanisms.what: The seam a renderer uses to read whole-session derived figures that paging and compaction cannot change. Units register on `ctx.sessionProjections` with a key, a stateVersion and a state schema, and are delivered through the registry snapshot, the change feed and every projection carrier. `session-stats` registers the `sessionStats` unit (stateVersion 1) folding turns/steps plus llmMs, toolMs, ttftMs, ttftSteps, decodeMs and decodeTokens from step/start, assistant/attempt and assistant/message; `token-meter` registers `tokenUsage` (stateVersion 2), `contextPressure` (stateVersion 4) and `contextBreakdown` (stateVersion 4). A registered key that is absent from the current cut means capability absent, not zero.
invariants: A unit's `apply` must return the same state reference for uninteresting events, because Object.is gates the change feed.
Client reads treat a missing key as capability absence (host unit unmounted, or no baseline/frame yet) and never invent a default value.
Durations are clamped with Math.max(0, ...) so clock skew cannot produce negative figures.
constants: sessionStats stateVersion = 1; tokenUsage stateVersion = 2; contextPressure stateVersion = 4; contextBreakdown stateVersion = 4

mechanisms.name: settings-seam
mechanisms.what: The settings seam the presentation layer configures through. `SettingsProvider` is an abstract Cordis Service registered as `ctx.settings` that owns namespace registration, resolution, validation, change detection and the `settings/updated` commit event; subclasses implement only `load()` and `persist()` and declare `writable`. Registrations produce a `SettingsScope<T>` with get/watch/update/replace. A conflicting write is signalled by `SettingsConflictError` carrying a stable `SETTINGS_CONFLICT` code plus expected/actual revisions. A redacted descriptor read (`describe({ redactSecrets })`) is the contract for configuration UIs, and path-addressed `SettingsPathOp` (`set`/`unset`) exists precisely because a UI holding a redacted view must not rebuild a section wholesale and silently delete secrets.
invariants: Paths are addressed against the section as stored, never against whatever the caller last read; writes are serialized per namespace by a write queue.
Teardown sets stopped, refusing new writes and new watchers, then settles every queued write chain and started watcher invocation before completing.
Namespace keys match /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/ and a `role('secret')` field must never appear in a redacted descriptor.

mechanisms.name: file-settings-provider
mechanisms.what: The shipped SettingsProvider implementation behind the seam: one YAML or JSON document (default `<harness home>/settings.yaml`) holds every namespace section. External edits hot-publish through a chokidar watcher with a write-settle window; the raw text of the last successful parse/persist is cached and a watcher event equal to that cache is a no-op, which is also the self-write suppression. Every write acquires a cross-process file lock, re-reads the document, and applies a leaf-level `setIn`/`deleteIn` diff so untouched nodes and the key node of every changed pair keep their comments, anchors and formatting. Files are created 0o600 in 0o700 directories, atomically.
invariants: Only .yaml/.yml/.json extensions are accepted; anything else fails at resolution time.
The watcher write-settle window and the chokidar poll interval derive from one `debounceMs` value; defaults are resolved in one `resolveSpec`, never inline.
A non-map value (array or scalar) replaces wholesale when unequal, taking interior comments with it.
constants: chokidar stabilityThreshold = debounceMs; pollInterval = max(1, min(debounceMs, 10))
file mode 0o600, directory mode 0o700; JSON indent 2

mechanisms.name: client-boot-manifest-announcement
mechanisms.what: The host-announced descriptor of what the presentation layer is composed of. The node half of `client/modules` scans the Loader's entries for packages declaring `dsh.client`, composes a content-addressed `WebBootGraph` (rev, entries, batches) and injects it into index.html as the `globalThis.__DSH_BOOT__` row plus parser-blocking bootstrap and preloaded application combo scripts; before that it installs a `window.__ModuleLoader__` queue shim so bundles registering early are not lost. The browser face parses the same wire into two consumer views — a module-table view (fetch the bundle) and a cordis-plugin view (compose the entry) — and the boot-readiness deferred `__DSH_BOOT_READY__` settles after the last injected row. `ctx.remote.$host` publishes the small fixed Host fact set (home, isLoopback) that a renderer may read without a subscription.
invariants: The wire is single-sourced: the host node half and the browser parser share one `WebBootEntry`/`WebBootGraph` shape.
A dynamic package row must precede rows whose `external` requests it; Cordis activation order is unrelated and stays with fiber service waiting.
A bundle factory executes only on first import/require and is memoized; script execution registers, it does not materialize.

mechanisms.name: directory-picker-capability-detection
mechanisms.what: Capability detection as a first-class seam: the directory-picker service exposes a discriminated `capability()` rather than a fixed method set, and every consumer switches on `capability().kind`. The auto chooser samples the host once at boot — bind host, SSH launch, platform, Linux chooser binaries (zenity/kdialog), DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY — and mounts the matching backend plus its browser surface as genuine Loader entries, unmounting the other pair. Anything ambiguous resolves to `browse`, the interaction that works for remote clients, and the documented default for an unknown kind is to hide the picking affordance instead of failing.
invariants: The capability object must be stable across calls for one service lifetime; consumers capture and compare it by reference.
A display-dependent backend is never mounted where no OS chooser can be reached (non-loopback bind, SSH launch, or no display).
An unknown capability kind hides the affordance; it is not an error.
constants: native is available only on darwin/win32/linux

mechanisms.name: acp-capability-advertisement
mechanisms.what: A second capability-negotiation seam: the ACP bridge advertises what it can actually do in the `initialize` response instead of assuming the client's. It reports the single PROTOCOL_VERSION, agentInfo, `mcpCapabilities: { http: true }`, `sessionCapabilities: { close, list, resume }` and `promptCapabilities: { image: <computed>, audio: false, embeddedContext: false }`. The image flag comes from `supportsAcpImagePrompts`, which returns false whenever the attachment store, the LLM service, the configured provider or the model is absent, when the deployment's accepted media types do not intersect the image types, or when the routed model's `inputModalities` does not include 'image' — unknown is negative by construction.
invariants: Absence of any input to the check (service, route, capability, deployment media support) resolves to false; the bridge never advertises a capability it cannot honour.
A single-version agent returns its one PROTOCOL_VERSION for both the 'same version if supported' and 'latest supported' branches.
The advertised capability gates prompt admission at runtime, so advertisement and enforcement read one value.
constants: agentCapabilities: mcpCapabilities.http = true; promptCapabilities.audio = false; promptCapabilities.embeddedContext = false; sessionCapabilities = { close, list, resume }

mechanisms.name: tool-presentation-mode-policy
mechanisms.what: dsh's screen/presentation-mode policy for the model-facing tool surface (the backend analogue of a UI screen mode). `ToolPresentationMode` is 'native' | 'ptc' | 'both': native sends every visible schema, ptc sends only `run_code` plus a generated SDK prompt and collapses the executor to that same surface, both sends both forms; ptc requires a mounted code runtime whose language has a registered SDK renderer, and native names in toolOrder are invalid under ptc. The mode is either the deployment default (the tools row's config field) or a scoped override via `tools.presentAs(mode)`, where the nearest scope on the chain wins so one agent preset can compose PTC agents beside native ones in the same process.
invariants: `presentAs` requires a scoped (agent.ctx) context; a process-global presentation is the config field instead.
One declaration per scope: a second presentAs for the same scope throws rather than silently composing.
Switching to ptc without a code runtime whose language has a registered SDK renderer fails prompt assembly instead of degrading silently.
constants: maxParallelSubCalls default 10 (must be a positive integer)

mechanisms.name: user-question-interaction-seam
mechanisms.what: The seam where an engine-side tool call blocks on a human. `UserQuestionService` (`super(ctx, 'userQuestions')`) validates the request — at least one question; when an agent is supplied it must be the registry's exact live instance and a runtime root, not an owned child — and then dispatches `user-questions/request` as an Agent-scoped Cordis waterfall whose default `next()` rejects with NO_PROVIDER. Presentation intents ('plan-review' etc.) are checked at the asker: the named approve label must be one of the question's own options and the reviewed detail must be present, so a UI honouring the intent can never show a choice the asker never offered. The event is forwarded to browser consumers through the allowlist's two waterfall entries.
invariants: Human interaction is gated by runtime ownership, not durable session lineage: a resumed session that is a new runtime root may ask; an owned child may not.
A presentation intent that names a non-option approve label, or omits the detail it reviews, is an error at the asker rather than in each UI.
The default answerer rejects; there is no implicit timeout answer.
constants: Error codes EMPTY_QUESTIONS, CALLER_NOT_LIVE, DELEGATED_CALLER, BAD_INTENT, NO_PROVIDER, ASK_ABORTED

mechanisms.name: session-telemetry-capture-seam
mechanisms.what: The capture side of session telemetry: a backend-agnostic Service Definition (`SessionTelemetryBackend`, registered as `ctx.sessionTelemetry`) plus the `SessionTelemetryCoordinator` a backend composes in its constructor. Ledger records mirror canonical session-log events one-to-one through live capture (session/created, session/event, session/disposed, session/flush plus the agent/error relay) or through on-demand replay of the canonical log; ops records ('agent-error', 'shutdown') carry no event identity. Every record is a deep clone of the event data, gets a pre-mapped severity (tool/result isError and turn/end error reasons become 'error'), minimal identity attributes, and passes through the `session-telemetry/record` waterfall that is the deployment's only redaction extension point. A module-scope WeakMap handoff cursor lets a re-adopting fiber resume instead of re-handing history.
invariants: `emit` must be a non-blocking enqueue: it is called synchronously from the session/event hot path, and its errors are contained and logged rather than reaching the agent loop.
The redaction waterfall ships no rules of its own; the innermost next() passes the record through, so exported data is exactly as clean as the rules a deployment mounts.
A throwing rule withholds that one record (containment is per event) and never starves later events in the same replay.
constants: Zero numeric constants in src/ (previously handed seq starts at -1 when history is excluded)

mechanisms.name: otel-telemetry-export
mechanisms.what: The shipped telemetry backend: it composes the OpenTelemetry JS SDK as-is — a LoggerProvider with a BatchLogRecordProcessor and an OTLPLogExporter — and maps each captured record onto `logger.emit()` with timestamp/observedTimestamp, the severity triple, the body as AnyValue and the identity attributes. Two sharing modes exist: FEEDBACK_ONLY (default) captures session history only when feedback is explicitly submitted and wires an on-demand coordinator with includeHistory; DISABLED constructs no SDK state at all and merely warns when recorded feedback stays local. Resource attributes carry service.name/service.version from APP_IDENTITY plus OTel's standard `user.id` from the anonymous-user-id package. The plugin owns one outer shutdown deadline because the SDK's export timeout does not bound its preceding forceFlush() wait.
invariants: Capture is authorized only by a listener that is the canonical appended event (session.eventAt(event.seq) === event); a non-canonical event warns and is dropped.
Only this Session's own explicit feedback authorizes replay — events below inheritedEventCount, and message-level events for another session, never do.
The optional flush() hint is deliberately not implemented, because forwarding it to forceFlush() would be the only source of concurrent flushes and can silently drop tail records.
constants: exporter.url is required outside DISABLED and must be http(s)

mechanisms.name: anonymous-identity-attribution
mechanisms.what: The per-harness-home anonymous identity shared by telemetry and feedback. `getOrCreateAnonymousUserId()` reads (or mints and persists) a random UUID v4 stored as a bare line in `.anonymous-user-id` inside the harness home resolved by resolveDshHome ($DSH_HOME, else ~/.dsh). The id is never derived from hostname, network address, git remote or any other identifying source; it is scoped to the harness home rather than the machine, so every process sharing one home reports the same id and deleting the file mints a fresh identity next launch. Reads and writes are synchronous and memoized per resolved file path; a concurrent first launch is settled by an exclusive-create write whose loser rereads the winner.
invariants: The id is a random UUID with no derivation from any identifying input; the file is the only storage and contains nothing but the UUID line.
Persistence is best-effort: a read-only home still yields a usable, process-consistent id so feedback and telemetry are never blocked.
One process touches the disk once; a file deleted mid-run keeps the process's id until the next launch.

mechanisms.name: invariant-runtime-diagnostics
mechanisms.what: A configurable registry of package-owned runtime invariant checks. Every package registers its checks from a `./invariant` companion through `ctx.invariants.register(packageName, installer)`, so ordinary package entrypoints stay independent of diagnostics; the registry installs each contribution into its own child fiber and binds a `fail` reporter that throws a package-attributed `InvariantError` carrying code 'INVARIANT' and the owning npm package name. Selection is a global `enabled` switch plus case-sensitive JavaScript regex allowlist and blocklist over package names; a filtered-out package still has its name reserved, so a duplicate registration throws either way.
invariants: A package name may be registered at most once, and the reservation survives filtering.
Package names must be non-blank and contain no whitespace; allow/blocklist entries must be non-blank, unwhitespaced, duplicate-free and valid regexes, or the registry construction throws.
An enabled installer that rejects disposes its child fiber and releases the reservation.
constants: Config defaults: enabled = true, package_allowlist = [], package_blocklist = []
Empty allowlist admits all; blocklist applies after allowlist matching

mechanisms.name: session-stats-projection
mechanisms.what: Whole-session accounting figures served through the session-projection seam rather than recomputed per render. The `session-stats` plugin registers one projection unit, `sessionStats` (stateVersion 1), that folds turn and step counts plus wall-time buckets: llmMs from step/start to the closing assistant/message, ttftMs/ttftSteps from the first streamed token, and decodeMs/decodeTokens gated on a provider-reported output token count. The plugin owns only the fold — delivery through the registry snapshot, the change feed and every projection carrier is the seam's job, so paging and compaction cannot change the figures a client renders.
invariants: Uninteresting events return the same state reference (Object.is gates the change feed).
One assembled assistant message closes one step boundary, so a defensive duplicate cannot accrue twice.
Every duration is clamped with Math.max(0, ...); decode metrics require a finite non-negative provider output count.
constants: initial totals all zero: turns, steps, llmMs, toolMs, ttftMs, ttftSteps, decodeMs, decodeTokens

mechanisms.name: token-and-cost-metering
mechanisms.what: Replay-aware token and cost accounting for request and surface pressure. `TokenMeter` (`super(ctx, 'tokenMeter')`) is the replay owner: it registers the tokenUsage/contextPressure/contextBreakdown projection units, lazily folds each Session's durable log through `_sync` up to `session.seq`, and answers `measure(session, requestHeader?)` with a deeply frozen, structured-cloned `TokenMeasurement` (baseline, surfaceDeltaTokens, totalTokens, surfaceTokens, nodes). A fixed heuristic prices messages (4 chars per token, 4-token block and role overheads); `priceSurface` replaces attachment heuristics with the routed model's actual image pricing and the mounted LLM service's file projection, and throws if the pricing answers a different occurrence count than it was asked, because misalignment would silently misprice. Provider usage is reused only when the latest successful call's canonical envelope matches and its total is no lower than the route-priced anchor.
invariants: No settings are supported: any key in TokenMeterConfig throws rather than being ignored.
Every fallible step (surface plan and anchor validation) runs before replay state mutates, so a malformed event stays unread on retry instead of half-applying.
measure() returns detached deeply immutable values; the internal fold is never aliased to a caller.
constants: Projection state versions: tokenUsage 2, contextPressure 4, contextBreakdown 4

mechanisms.name: message-feedback-ledger
mechanisms.what: Durable per-message feedback stored in the canonical session log rather than a side store. `MessageFeedbackService` (`super(ctx, 'messageFeedback')`) exposes three Remote methods — list, put and delete — that derive current state by replaying `feedback/message-put` / `feedback/message-delete` events for the target session. Writes are optimistic-concurrency controlled by an item `version` UUID (`ifVersion` must equal the current version or null), a matching no-op retains the version and appends no event, and notes are bounded by a deployment-required `maxNoteBytes`. Cold operations hold write ownership across read/compare/append and never construct a Session or Agent; live operations go through the live owner and then verify the appended prefix is actually durable before acknowledging. A `feedback/committed` parallel event lets observers see a committed cold mutation without publishing a live Session.
invariants: A put only targets a message that exists as an append-surface assistant/message event in the log; otherwise it is target-not-found.
Operations are serialized per session id and drained on disposal; a new mutation after disposal begins is rejected.
maxNoteBytes is required with no default and must be a positive safe integer.
constants: maxNoteBytes: required, no default, positive safe integer
timestamps bounded by Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER; version is a UUID
Failure codes: session-not-found, target-not-found, version-conflict, note-blank, note-too-large

mechanisms.name: session-feedback-command-and-remote
mechanisms.what: The human feedback channel. One closed category vocabulary (`FEEDBACK_CATEGORIES`, seven entries in presentation order) is exported for product surfaces, `recordFeedback(session, entry)` appends exactly one log-only `feedback/record` event with trimmed text and an optional category, and the same operation is exposed as a Typert Remote (`SessionFeedbackService`, `super(ctx, 'sessionFeedback')`, `@Remote('record')`) so a product surface records without a slash command. A `/feedback <text>` command is registered on the shared command registry as the human-facing entry point, and its acknowledgement names both the receiving session and the anonymous user id. Recording never starts model work.
invariants: An entry with neither text nor category is still recorded; surrounding whitespace is discarded and a blank text is recorded as absent.
The Remote reports `session-not-found` for an unknown live session; it never creates a session.
The command result is an error (with usage text) when no feedback text was supplied, and in that case no event is appended.
constants: FEEDBACK_CATEGORIES = task-result, instruction-following, product-interaction, service-stability, resource-cost, security-privacy-permission, other

mechanisms.name: runtime-inspector-diagnostics
mechanisms.what: An experimental out-of-repo diagnostics plane: a host plugin (`name = 'experimental-inspector'`, inject ['webServer']) starts a loopback HTTP + WebSocket inspector worker (port 9230 by default, occupied ports advance) and injects a client bootstrap into index.html; a browser-face plugin (inject []) provides the same `ctx.inspector` service and publishes JSON observations with a topic, a validated payload and a monotonic timestamp. The package implements a Chrome-DevTools-Protocol-shaped surface (runtime, debugger, DOM, network, sources domains over mirrored host/client realms) plus read-only Cordis runtime-tree queries, and carries more than twenty explicit memory/lifecycle bounds. Every bound is configurable and defaults come from one `resolveInspectorOptions()` call, so the schema and the library cannot drift.
invariants: Observation payloads are validated as JSON before entering the carrier; publish() does not wait for worker delivery.
The endpoint binds only 127.0.0.1 and admits only explicitly listed client origins.
Cordis tree snapshots are depth-capped and scoped: process-global inspection is not part of the client realm contract.
constants: port default 9230 (max 65535); host fixed '127.0.0.1'; captureFetch default true
maxRequestBodyBytes 8 MiB; maxResponseBodyBytes 32 MiB; maxBodyChunkBytes 48 KiB; maxJournalBytes 256 MiB

mechanisms.name: performance-benchmark-budgets
mechanisms.what: A source-only benchmark suite that pins cold-path and long-session performance as CI assertions rather than as reports. Six suites exist: session-open (isolated built-worker measurement of open/read/sessionRestore/projection phases, first Host history and cold Agent resume, plus a constrained-heap run), agent-continuation (request-history, tool-continuation, child-catalog and profile-continuation scenarios over an 800-turn synthetic workload), a synthetic-history seed-correctness bench, conversation-fold (compiled cold client conversation fold over a 500,000-delta window), long-session-browser (Playwright/Chromium open, paging, trajectory switch, first token, streaming responsiveness, heap and DOM node count over 240 turns) and active-stream-reconnect (ClientAssistantStream.replace over a 100,000-delta live prefix). Budgets are reference-machine durations converted by a shared calibration helper, and each suite re-asserts its own computed budget so a silent recalibration fails.
invariants: Every timed benchmark runs in a freshly built worker (`.dsh-build/**/*.js`) with NODE_OPTIONS and TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH stripped; the runtime guard rejects tsx loaders and package entries outside lib/**/*.js.
CI budgets are derived, never hand-written: ciTimeBudget(expected) = ceil(expected * CI_TIME_SCALE * PERFORMANCE_BUDGET_HEADROOM).
A stuck worker is SIGKILLed at the suite's own timeout (60 s for the heavy suites, 30 s for the browser/worker client suites).

mechanisms.name: fail-loud-crash-handling
mechanisms.what: Crash and fatal-failure handling on the service side. `installFailLoud` is installed before boot and turns a late unhandled plugin-init rejection into one labelled stderr diagnostic plus exit(1); a rejection already accounted for by the activation audit is ignored during its process checkpoint. The exit is deliberately deferred through an optional `release` hook raced against FAIL_LOUD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT_MS, so a terminal-owning surface can hand the terminal back; the handler stays installed during the release and a latch keeps the first rejection the reported one. `assertEntriesLoaded`/`assertEntriesActivated` then audit the settled Loader and fail startup when a non-disabled entry has no fiber. The web server adds a last-resort per-request guard that logs and answers 400 instead of letting one malformed request become an unhandled rejection, and the SDK client retains a bounded stderr tail to diagnose an unexpected runtime death.
invariants: The diagnostic is written before the release runs, so a hanging disposer cannot swallow the reason.
The fatal exit is never cancelled by a wedged disposer — only delayed up to the release timeout; the timer stays referenced so Node cannot reach an empty event loop and exit 0.
A per-request failure must never exit the process: once headers are sent the response is destroyed, otherwise a 400 is written.
constants: Fiber state mirrors FIBER_PENDING = 0, FIBER_ACTIVE = 2, FIBER_FAILED = 3
last-resort HTTP status 400 (or response destroy after headers)

mechanisms.name: profile-distribution-and-module-fallback
mechanisms.what: Distribution, layout and update semantics of a dsh installation. Each profile is a directory under `<harness home>/profiles/<name>` whose manifest lists an ordered bundle layer array plus a user patch layer (`cordis.patch.yml`); `PROFILE_TEMPLATES` ships five templates (acp, web, headless, sdk, sdk-minimal) with a per-profile patch reload policy — 'live' only for web, 'startup' for everything else — and an installation-owned tuple map lets a shipped template be normalized after upgrade. Profiles are made resolvable through symlinked private package links in a `.dsh-module-fallback` directory that is healed on load, so a profile keeps working when the checkout layout or package manager store changes. `resolveDshHome` anchors all of this under $DSH_HOME or ~/.dsh.
invariants: The user patch layer is applied after every bundle layer, and its reload policy is a property of the profile template rather than of the file.
Custom profiles with no shipped template retain the historical live patch reload and default to the '@deepseek-ai/dsh-base' bundle list.
Module-fallback links are installation-owned and healed (not trusted) at load; a manifest that no longer matches is rewritten.
constants: PROFILE_TEMPLATES: acp = [dsh-base, dsh-acp-app] startup; web = [dsh-base, dsh-web-app] live; headless = [dsh-base, dsh-headless] startup; sdk = [dsh-base, dsh-sdk-app] startup; sdk-minimal = [dsh-sdk-minimal] startup

notes: Scope: three domains of the dsh v0.1.5-rc.2 source tree at D:\agent-complete\deepseek-harness-dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2, read-only; nothing in that tree was modified. Every 'evidence' entry is a path:line or path:line-line that this agent opened with the read tool, so all mechanisms are verified:true. Line numbers are 1-based against the file as read. Build tooling that is not a Cordis row (typert/generator's rolldown plugin) is recorded as a mechanism because it produces the wire artifacts the RPC plane dispatches against. Two capabilities were found to exist with no in-tree production caller or no production caller at all in this composition: (a) `typert-descriptor-codegen`'s loader half only activates for packages that declare `exports["./typert"]` and is additionally driven by the optional `packages` config list; (b) `runtime-inspector-diagnostics` is explicitly experimental (plugin name 'experimental-inspector') and its host endpoint is not mounted by any of the five shipped profiles in PROFILE_TEMPLATES. `client/hmr` is a development-only reload chain and is deliberately not counted as a mechanism. Mechanism counts per domain: service 15, interface 12, ops 12; the service domain is one above the requested 8-14 aim because service-self-auth-token-cookie and browser-trust-fence were kept separate from browser-http-api-transport (distinct failure policies: 401 vs 403) and because webhook-ingress-and-verification is an unauthenticated HMAC ingress rather than a browser transport. moduleCoverage repeats the complete required module list in each of the three domains so no module is omitted from any domain; entries beginning with 'no ...-domain mechanism' or 'presentation plugin' are the one-line reasons. The requested 'client/ui-sidebar*' wildcard is answered by one entry covering client/ui-sidebar, client/ui-sidebar-files, client/ui-sidebar-right and client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview, and client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview is additionally keyed explicitly. 'sdk/client' appears twice in the required list and is covered once. The requested 'screen-mode policy' has no UI-screen-mode service in dsh; the closest engine-side policy seam is ToolPresentationMode ('native' | 'ptc' | 'both') with the scoped tools.presentAs() override, recorded as tool-presentation-mode-policy.
